Discriminating check — a module-level importorskip was tried first and silently skipped the integrity layer too (1 skipped, 0 passed): F0 would have reported green while proving nothing. Moved into _cleaning_service() so integrity always executes.

Gate proven to bite, not just report green: deleting remove_outlier_iqr.json -> test_index_lists_every_case FAILS; nulling one expected value -> test_fixture_is_well_formed[drop_missing] FAILS. Regenerating restored both, which also re-proves determinism.

Row-count deltas confirm real semantics: drop_missing 40->31, drop_single_tag 40->32, precleanse_time_crop 40->21, and precleanse_conditional_drop stays 40 because that action deletes the CELL not the row — the quirk Python must not 'fix'.
pytest==9.1.1 added to apps/python/requirements.txt (test-only; no runtime import touched).

REVIEW FIX 1 — ragged missingness. The first cut marked non-Good rows by index alone (i%11, i%13), so ALL tags shared one mask and FI-404 was a strict subset of the others. drop_missing could not then distinguish a correct union-across-tags from an implementation reusing one tag's mask for every column. Status offsets are now per-tag (tagIndex*3); all three tag pairs differ in BOTH directions, and drop_missing went 40->31 to 40->19 (21 rows = the true union). A new test asserts raggedness so it cannot silently regress.

REVIEW FIX 2 — float comparison. The parity assertion compared floats with exact ==, against JSON numbers the browser produced via Math.round(v*10**p)/10**p. Python's 72.1+0.1+0.2 = 72.39999999999999 != 72.4 and 119.99999999999999 != 120, so F2 would have shown false parity failures. frame_to_wide now rounds to the fixture's per-tag precision, matching preprocessing.ts:506. test_round_trip_survives_float_noise proves it WITHOUT the F2 service, so the guarantee holds today rather than being discovered later.
Checked and NOT an issue: `from conftest import` also resolves when pytest runs from the repo root (pytest inserts the test dir into sys.path) — 95 passed from both cwds.

features.title: Cleaning operations (parity-gated)
features.description: The op registry restricted to what the client already implements, so every op is parity-testable against F0 fixtures.
features.note: Scoped to the OPERATIONS ENGINE plus the HTTP surface that F3 needed. cleaning_service.py (registry + apply_operations), schemas/preprocess.py and routers/preprocess.py all exist and are parity-green. The /materialize, /clean and /rows endpoints moved to F4, where the job runner is the thing that actually calls them — the plan always said they 'land with F4', and leaving F2 open for them made F3 a completed feature hanging off an incomplete dependency.
verificationResults: services/cleaning_service.py: CLEANING_OPS registry keyed by the browser's own CleaningMethod names, so a saved recipe replays without translation, plus OPERATION_ALIASES mapping the public request shape (drop_missing / fill_missing{ffill,bfill,mean,median,constant,linear} / remove_outlier{zscore,iqr} / clip / smooth{moving_avg,exponential}) onto them.

ALL 20 preprocessPipelines parity fixtures pass as REAL assertions (verified per-fixture with -v, not silent skips). The 3 precleanse fixtures skip by design: its 'drop' DELETES a single tag's cell, which a rectangular frame cannot express without a fourth 'absent' status — deferred rather than faked.

HARNESS BUG, NOT A PORT BUG: fill_missing_mean and fill_missing_linear failed at first because the F0 review fix rounded ALL comparison output to per-tag precision. The client's FILLS DO NOT ROUND — only the outlier/smoothing ops do — so the fixture legitimately expects 81.05937499999999 and the harness forced it to 81.1. frame_to_wide no longer rounds; comparison moved to assert_grids_match with rel_tol=1e-9 / abs_tol=1e-12. Three tests assert the tolerance still fails on a value change, a status flip, and a row-count change.

CRITICAL FINDING — the golden fixtures alone do NOT discriminate the quirks. A sabotage probe injecting four deliberate regressions caught only 1 of 4: banker's rounding, numpy.quantile quartiles, and sample-vs-population std all slipped through the 40-row fixtures, because on that data the alternatives classify the same cells. The suite was giving false confidence; anyone later 'tidying' the port into idiomatic numpy would have seen no failure.

FIX: tests/test_cleaning_quirks.py pins each quirk directly on inputs where the alternatives PROVABLY differ — the IQR test uses [1..7, 12] because 12 sits inside the floor-index fence (13.0) but outside numpy's (11.5); a far-out value like 100 is flagged by both and proves nothing. Each pin also asserts the substitute really differs so it cannot rot into a tautology. Re-running the sabotage probe now catches 4 of 4.

Quirks ported and pinned: JS Math.round half-up (Python's round is banker's — 2.5 -> 3, not 2); population std in zscore vs sample std in precleanse; floor-index quartiles; zscore REPLACES with the mean rather than removing; fills do not round while outlier/smoothing ops do; forward/backward fill flips status to Good even with no donor; drop marks rows across every tag and removes the union once at the end.

remove_duplicates has no browser counterpart and so no fixture: defined here as whole-frame keep-first on timestamp, explicitly NOT data_service._dedupe (which dedupes on the timestamp STRING at batch-window boundaries).

REVIEW FIX — apply_operations (the request-shaped entry point F4 will call) had ZERO coverage: every parity guarantee ran through preprocess_pipelines, so the endpoint could have shipped on an unverified path. Added tests proving the two routes produce identical frames, that unknown tags are rejected on every operation INCLUDING remove_duplicates (which is frame-wide and previously accepted a typo'd tag silently), that unsupported/typeless operations raise, and that operations chain in order.

REVIEW FIX — param aliasing precedence was decided by dict iteration order, so a caller sending both `window` and `threshold` got an invisible rule. Extracted to _PARAM_ALIASES, ordered highest-precedence first and documented; a test pins that explicit `param` beats the friendly aliases and that clip accepts both min/max and paramLow/param spellings.

EMERGENT BEHAVIOUR DOCUMENTED AND PINNED: zscore derives mean/std from Good cells but tests EVERY cell (faithful to the client). Combined with frame_service storing holes as 0.0/Bad, a hole among readings near 72 scores as a huge outlier, so zscore replaces it with the mean and marks it Good — it imputes. The browser never produced this because its Bad cells hold plausible values, not zeros. Verified live and pinned by test_zscore_imputes_a_bad_hole so it stays a decision rather than a surprise.

Final sabotage re-run on the strengthened suite: JS-vs-banker's rounding CAUGHT, population-vs-sample std CAUGHT, floor-index-vs-numpy quartiles CAUGHT. Honest caveat: swapping only q1 while leaving q3 floor-indexed is NOT caught — a mixed-definition fence that no realistic refactor produces, noted rather than over-engineered.

features.securityFinding: CONFIRMED AND FIXED, found while building /materialize. FastAPI's default RequestValidationError handler returns exc.errors() verbatim, and every pydantic v2 error carries the failing value under `input`. A malformed /v1/preprocess/materialize body answered 422 with the DECRYPTED password in plaintext; python-client.ts relays an upstream 4xx `detail` onward as an AppException message, so it reaches the browser. Verified by request before and after. The same leak existed on the pre-existing /v1/data-sources/* routes, which take the same credential blocks — the handler is app-wide and tests/test_error_redaction.py asserts all four endpoints. Also made the preprocess 502 branch generic: an unexpected PI/SQL driver exception can embed a connection string, and that branch used to interpolate the exception text.
pythonVerification: tests/test_artifact_service.py — 16 tests over a RecordingStore that reproduces the real store's immutability refusal, since the runner depends on that behaviour when it writes its final step to the committed version key.

Pinned refusals: clean will not overwrite a committed version, may rewrite its own tmp step on retry, rejects target==source, surfaces a missing source instead of writing an empty target, and FAILS a pipeline that drops every row (an empty frame is legal Parquet, so without the guard the job would succeed and commit rowCount 0).
cleanup refuses any prefix outside tmp/ and any prefix without a trailing slash — 'ds-1/tmp/job-1' would otherwise also match 'ds-1/tmp/job-10/'.
materialize pins the routing decision (exactly one of pi/sql) because both 'neither' and 'both' have plausible wrong answers: write an empty artifact, or silently prefer one source.

features.designNotes: materialize takes CREDENTIALS + fetch params, not rows: NestJS fetching and forwarding millions of rows as JSON would move the browser's memory ceiling onto the API server instead of removing it. Reuses the credential contract /v1/data-sources/* already uses. Commit path: the last operation writes straight to the committed version key with overwrite=false, then the $transaction. No promote/copy endpoint — it would double the I/O for a window that cannot be closed anyway. Two consequences: a retry MUST mint a new versionId (the old key may exist and is immutable), and a crash between the write and the transaction leaves an orphan object.

deferred: Parquet row-group pushdown in ObjectStore.get_frame_slice/get_frame_head: both read the whole object then slice, so the preview's sample cap bounds COMPUTE, not I/O. Measured fine today (0.60s at 10M rows on local MinIO) — the binding constraint is resident memory and link speed to storage, not the 30s timeout. Revisit when artifacts outgrow memory or storage moves off the local network.

Concurrent preview memory: asyncio.to_thread introduced real concurrency where the event loop previously serialised previews. The measured 0.60s/10M-row figure is SINGLE-REQUEST; resident cost is ~800MB per in-flight preview against one lru_cached ObjectStore, so N concurrent large previews multiply it. A semaphore is the fix when it matters; concurrent footprint has not been measured.

ColumnStats.count is TOTAL rows and `missing` is separate, so good = count - missing. The other plausible reading (count = non-null observations, total = count + missing) yields a wrong '% good'. Self-consistent today because missing_pct == missing/count*100, but F4 zod-parses this shape and F5 renders it — pin it with a field description before either lands.

findings: PreprocessingJob progress fields (progress/currentStep/totalSteps/completedSteps/estimatedRemainingMs) do NOT match the client's FetchProgress (totalBatches/completedBatches/currentBatchTags/totalTags/completedTags/etaMs/failedBatches). The plan claimed they were the same fields; they are not — FetchProgress is tag-batch-shaped for PI fetching, job progress is operation-shaped. F5 needs a thin adapter. Reusing the progress UI COMPONENT does not require identical field names, so the DB model was left alone rather than contorted.

SQL materialize is bounded at 50,000 rows by SQLQueryRequest.limit (le=50000), which is the pre-existing /sql/query cap, not something this slice introduced. PI materialize has no such cap. Raise it deliberately if SQL sources need to exceed that.
